title: An Identity minted from a user URI must be writable on the wire
description:
Nothing between an MLS credential and the IRC wire keeps a user URI writable.
`parse_user_uri` (crates/mimid-agent-irc/src/names.rs) rejects an empty
domain, an empty local part and a `/` in the local part, and nothing else;
`user_uri_domain` (crates/mimid-agent-core/src/uri.rs) rejects `/`, `?` and
`#`; neither checks the domain for a space or a control character, and neither
bounds the length. `Names::identity` copies the string it is given into
`Identity.uri`, and `base_identity` falls back to `("unknown.invalid",
"user")` for anything that is not `mimi://<domain>/u/<local>` without
rejecting it.

The URI is then written raw in three places, each of which a peer can
therefore split or lengthen past 512 octets:

- 330 RPL_WHOISACCOUNT, where it is a middle parameter
  (crates/mimid-agent-irc/src/command.rs, the `whois` numerics);
- 311 RPL_WHOISUSER's `<realname>`;
- 352 RPL_WHOREPLY's `0 <uri>`.

Bead mimid-1wgh.140.6 guarded the two lines it added — extended-join's
account and realname parameters and the `account` tag — with `account_of`,
`account_param` and `MAX_ACCOUNT` in names.rs (decision mimid-1wgh.150). That
is a guard at the point of writing, repeated per site. The invariant belongs
where an `Identity` is minted, so that `Identity.uri` is writable by
construction and all of these sites are covered at once, with a named length
limit and a test at and past it.

Two things found while reading, which belong here:

- NICK takes any non-empty parameter (crates/mimid-agent-irc/src/register.rs,
  `fn nick`), so `NICK :foo bar` makes the burst's NICK line's source
  `foo bar!user@host` and splits that line.
- `Identity` has no constructor that can fail, so nothing in the type says
  where the check happened.
notes:
2026-11-28, from the parameter-grammar fix on branch irc-verbs (design
note agent-frontends.md §7.41):

Closed here, so this bead is narrower than it reads above.
- No parameter reaches the wire holding CR, LF or NUL, and no parameter
  that is not the last one reaches it empty, holding a space or
  beginning with `:`. Out::to_wire writes a space for each of the three
  in a last parameter and `*` for a middle one that could not be one, so
  330's middle parameter can no longer split a line or shift the
  parameters after it, whatever a peer puts in the URI.
- 401, 402, 406, the 369 after a 406, 421 and FAIL MONITOR bound the
  name they echo to line::MAX_ECHO (= names::MAX_ACCOUNT) and answer `*`
  past it.

Still open, and now the whole of this bead.
- Length. The URI is written at its own length in 311's and 314's
  <realname>, 312, 330, 352 and every hostmask, so one past MAX_ACCOUNT
  carries that reply past 512 octets. Those sites use Session::numeric,
  which does not cut. This is the invariant-at-minting half: an Identity
  whose uri is writable by construction covers all of them at once.
- The source, which to_wire writes raw and which no guard covers.
  Verified today: register.rs's NICK arm is
  `line.param(0).filter(|n| !n.is_empty())` with no is_nick check, and
  that string becomes the source of the burst NICK line
  (register.rs:478-486, sent when the asked nick differs from the one
  given). So `NICK :foo bar` makes the source `foo bar!user@host` and
  the client reads `bar!user@host` as the command; `NICK :a<CR>b` puts a
  CR mid-line. Reachable only by the connection's own client, and only
  after it has shown a credential, since the burst is registration's.
  to_wire cannot fix this one: a prefix holding a space or a CR has no
  safe substitute at that layer, because every octet of it is the
  identity. The fix is is_nick at the NICK arm.
